text:
Alicia Perez: dropping early mocks for Suggestions list + detail drawer. main questions i need input on:
1) where should the risk chip live (table vs drawer vs both)
2) drawer hierarchy (savings first vs what-to-change first)
3) disclaimer/copy: how explicit do we get about “estimated” + confidence?

figma: https://figma.com/file/RI-Console-Suggestions-beta?node-id=188%3A2041
linear: DES-188 https://linear.app/redwood/issue/DES-188

Current layout:
- table columns: Suggestion, Scope (route/model/region), Est. savings (monthly), Risk
- click row opens right drawer: header (suggestion title + risk chip), then “What changes” / “Why this helps” / “Estimated impact” / “Basis of estimate”

Tessa Morgan: thanks. overall direction feels good. my immediate take: risk chip should be visible in the list (so ppl can triage) AND repeated in drawer header. otherwise it’s too easy to click into something “High” by accident and feel surprised.

Kenji Nakamura: +1 on list + drawer. but careful about visual weight. if we put colored risk chips everywhere it might feel like a warning product.
maybe list shows a neutral label (Low/Med/High) and only drawer uses the more explicit colored chip? or make High more saturated and Low very muted.

Marissa Cole: PM view: need risk in list for “trust.” CS/SE will use list view in onboarding and they asked for quick scanning.
for drawer hierarchy i’d vote: start with “what to change” (actionability), then “estimated impact” (why they should care), then “why this helps” (explain), then “basis/assumptions” (trust) + disclaimer.

Aditya Rao: i’m aligned on risk showing in list. also want disclaimer visible without scrolling to the very bottom. we’re already getting questions about “are these guaranteed” from preview calls.
maybe a small “Estimates, not guarantees” helper text under the savings number?

Svetlana Orlov: design system note: we already have a Chip component with severity variants (neutral/info/warn/danger). if we map risk:
- Low = neutral
- Medium = warn
- High = danger
it’s consistent with existing patterns.
but we should avoid using the same red as “incident” in other parts of Console.

Dylan Brooks: from eng side: list row height is tight. if we add helper text under savings and a chip we might wrap in weird ways on smaller widths.
also: we can render risk in list and drawer easily; just want a decision on whether we need tooltip content in list (e.g. the rationale bullets) or only in drawer.

Alicia Perez: good call. right now i have a tooltip on risk chip in list (hover) that says “Potential impact to latency/quality and reversibility” + “See details.” but it’s vague.
Do we want to show the first rationale bullet in the tooltip? (e.g. “Limited latency headroom in us-east”) or keep rationale only in drawer.

Chloe Martin: please keep rationale out of the list tooltip if possible. we can’t guarantee we always have non-confusing bullets at v1, and we’ll get into truncation/formatting issues.
Drawer can show the rationale bullets with full context.

George Mbatha: jumping in from research angle: in early tests, folks interpret a risk label without rationale as “vendor covering themselves.” they immediately look for “why is it high?”.
that said, list tooltip might be too shallow. repeating risk + rationale in drawer header area seems most important.

Tessa Morgan: ^ agree. i’d rather keep list clean + force the “why” into drawer in a predictable spot.
proposal:
- list shows Risk chip (Low/Medium/High) + simple tooltip “Risk reflects potential impact to latency/quality/SLO and reversibility. Open for details.”
- drawer: risk chip + “Why this risk” section with 2–4 bullets near top (not buried)

Kenji Nakamura: yes. and i’d reorder drawer like:
1) Header: title + risk
2) “Recommended change” (what to do)
3) “Estimated savings” (with range + confidence language)
4) “Why this risk” (rationale bullets)
5) “Why this helps” (mechanism)
6) “Basis of estimate” (telemetry + assumptions + last updated)

i know Marissa said action first which i agree with. just think “why this risk” should sit close to savings so ppl can weigh tradeoff.

Marissa Cole: that ordering works for me if “why this risk” stays concise.
Also: can we standardize savings language? i don’t want “up to $X” marketing vibes.
maybe:
- “Estimated savings: $420–$610 / month”
- subtext “Based on last 7 days traffic. May vary with workload.”

Aditya Rao: +1. and we should avoid implying causality if they haven’t applied anything (since beta is read-only). language should be “could save” not “will save.”

Alicia Perez: on disclaimer: where do we put it so it’s seen but not obnoxious?
Option A: tiny grey line under savings in list (“Estimates based on recent usage”)
Option B: list is clean; drawer has an info callout under “Estimated savings”

Dylan Brooks: A is hard in table due to density. B is much easier and less clutter. we can add an info icon next to “Estimated savings” label too.

Svetlana Orlov: pattern: we have an inline “HelperText” component under section headers in drawers. could do:
Estimated savings
Helper text: “Estimates are based on recent metering and may vary. Not guaranteed.”

Kenji Nakamura: pls don’t bury the “not guaranteed” only in helper text. maybe bold “Estimated” in label + helper text covers the rest.
like “Estimated savings” as the header already signals it.

Tessa Morgan: let’s keep disclaimer consistent across list + drawer and across hosted/dedicated/private.
My vote: list column says “Est. savings” (already implies estimate) and drawer has helper text that includes “Not guaranteed” + a “Learn how this is calculated” link that jumps to Basis section.

George Mbatha: if we add the “Learn how calculated” link, it also reduces support load (“where did this number come from”). good.

Alicia Perez: ok. last open question: in list, do we show risk chip before savings or after? right now risk is last column.

Marissa Cole: keep risk last. people sort by savings first, then sanity check risk.

Kenji Nakamura: agree. also for scanning, savings is numeric and aligns well; risk chip at end is clear.

Chloe Martin: note: API will send risk_level + rationale bullets + “confidence score” for savings estimate (per ADR/contract). do we want to show confidence separately? i’ve seen product debate this.

Tessa Morgan: for now, no separate “confidence” badge in list. it’s too much.
In drawer we can optionally show a line like “Confidence: Medium” BUT only if we have strong definitions.
Otherwise, collapse confidence into the Basis section (e.g. “Confidence is lower when telemetry is sparse”).

Aditya Rao: +1. we can revisit after beta feedback. we already have risk taxonomy; adding confidence might confuse (users will ask “why is risk low but confidence low?”).

Alicia Perez: great. action items:
- update drawer hierarchy per Kenji/Tessa suggestion
- risk chip in list + repeated in drawer header
- add “Why this risk” block near top with rationale bullets
- disclaimer: keep list “Est. savings”; drawer helper text includes “not guaranteed” + jump link to Basis

i’ll post updated mock today.

(Linear Bot): Alicia Perez moved DES-188 to In Review.

Svetlana Orlov: when you update, ping me if you need final token mapping for chips + helper text styles. also watch contrast on Medium/High chips (a11y).

Dylan Brooks: thanks. once mock is updated, can you call out min drawer width? we’re trying to avoid horizontal scroll for the “basis” JSON-y stuff.

Alicia Perez: yep. i’ll cap the “basis” content into bullet rows (Telemetry window, Baseline $/1M tokens, Assumptions, Last updated) instead of raw JSON.

Tessa Morgan: :thumbsup: and pls add an empty state in the mock too (no suggestions / insufficient telemetry) so we can align on messaging.

Alicia Perez: will do.

Alicia Perez: updated frames are in figma (same link) under “v0.2”.
Changes:
- drawer order: Recommended change → Estimated savings (with helper + jump link) → Why this risk → Why this helps → Basis of estimate
- risk chip repeated in header + list
- “Why this risk” uses 3 bullets max
- added empty states (No suggestions yet / Insufficient data)

would love quick gut check on the empty state copy.

George Mbatha: empty state “Insufficient data” is good, but add one line: what they can do. something like “Check again after 24h of traffic, or ensure metering is enabled for this route.”
Otherwise they feel stuck.

Marissa Cole: +1. also avoid blaming language (“you haven’t configured…”). keep it neutral.

Tessa Morgan: looks solid. let’s take this direction into the DES-188 review tomorrow. thanks all.
